RP32 approval disposition — REJECTED FOR THIS JANITOR RUN, NOT PERMANENTLY.

False-positive assessment: replacing whole-document word checks with exact clauses or heading-scoped prose parsing can fail on behavior-neutral edits such as wrapping, Markdown emphasis, heading changes, or equivalent wording. Synonym regexes reduce only some coupling and cannot reliably determine natural-language polarity.

False-negative assessment: anchoring one authoritative section does not detect a contradictory restatement elsewhere. The present broad keyword checks do not solve that problem: unrelated or stale words anywhere in the same document can keep the test green after the governing instruction is reversed. Current maintained scope includes two trust-boundary statements (docs/output-schemas.md:156-160 and docs/event-schema.md:339-345) and the complete downgrade operational contract (docs/concurrency.md:508-523).

Future revisit bar: separate the precise source-of-truth contract from broad consistency discovery. Evaluate an explicit stable policy identifier or generated normative block that tolerates formatting-only edits; enumerate every intentional normative site; add reversal, distractor-keyword, and harmless-formatting controls; and state how contradictory noncanonical prose is found without making incidental mentions blocking failures. A repository-wide word scan may be advisory discovery, not semantic proof.

The full assessment is recorded under RP32 in .joe-janitor/report-2026-08-29.md. RP32 is excluded from this run's cleanup epic. No known-fine entry is added so a future Janitor run can re-examine it.

## Context

Run the rebar-janitor codebase-health pipeline against the current rebar repository as a deliberate maintenance pause. This is a read-only audit of product code: the deliverables are durable audit artifacts, a human-approved remediation plan, and tracker tickets. No production or test code will be changed.

## Scope

Inspect the repository for code debt, code and architectural smells, separation-of-concerns problems, spent optionality, documentation gaps, oversized units, weak test oracles, AI-generated-code and security smells, and temporal decay. Weight recently changed regions while covering the full codebase. Consult prior janitor artifacts, tickets, ADRs, and commit history so intentional decisions are not mistaken for defects.

This repository's established artifact location is `.joe-janitor/`: `docs/documentation-policy.md` explicitly recognizes that tree, and `.joe-janitor/tools.md` already contains the durable playbook. Reuse that location rather than the generic skill default.

## Plan

1. Discovery: fan out one concern per independent agent, shard comment and test-suite review by subsystem, and pool path:line-cited findings without severity or confidence.
2. Verification: independently blue-team each finding, establish reachable harm, check prior decisions and known-fine entries, apply the skill's fixed validity and impact floors, and persist the audit record plus reusable tool playbook.
3. Remediation: obtain two blind proposals per survivor from asymmetric evidence bases (community practice versus project record), converge at move/end-state level, and research divergences.
4. Approval: present the Remediation Plan one item at a time for human approve/refine/reject decisions; record explicit known-fine blessings only when given.
5. Ticketization: first search for a matching current Janitor Cleanup epic and children; create only missing tracker records. Approved work becomes actionable child tickets with acceptance criteria, provenance, dependencies, and file impact.

Any failed discovery shard remains an explicit coverage gap and prevents Phase 1 completion. Audit artifact updates preserve existing content and ticketization searches before creating records so a resumed run does not silently lose coverage or duplicate work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Discovery covers every concern required by the rebar-janitor skill.
- [ ] Every discovery candidate has an exact path:line citation.
- [ ] Discovery candidates contain no severity or confidence score.
- [ ] Independent verification records validity for every candidate it processes.
- [ ] Independent verification records impact and a reachable-harm statement for every candidate it processes.
- [ ] Independent verification records prior-decision and known-fine handling.
- [ ] Candidates below validity 0.75 are dropped.
- [ ] Candidates below impact 0.5 are dropped.
- [ ] The dated audit record is persisted at `.joe-janitor/report-2026-08-29.md`.
- [ ] The reusable command and pattern playbook is appended at `.joe-janitor/tools.md`.
- [ ] The audit report records commands and tuned thresholds.
- [ ] The audit report records survivors, dropped candidates, and their evidence-backed disposition.
- [ ] Every surviving finding receives two blind asymmetric-evidence remediation proposals.
- [ ] Every divergent proposal pair is researched before its item enters the Remediation Plan.
- [ ] Each remediation item receives an explicit user approve, refine, or reject decision before ticket creation.
- [ ] Approved work is filed as child tickets under a current Janitor Cleanup epic.
- [ ] Each created child is linked back to this audit ticket.
- [ ] No production code, tests, configuration, or documentation outside `.joe-janitor/` and the tracker is modified.
